mutants.expected_detection: Behavioral key-sweep test: for a fixed plaintext, invoking crypto_kernel with >=200 keys including key[0]==0 will show status_out flipping to 1 for that edge-case key while all other keys yield the correct XOR-fold checksum, violating SR1's requirement that status_out be invariant across keys and equal to the plaintext checksum.

Behavioral key-sweep test with fixed plaintext: for keys where key[0]==0, iter_count_out will be reported as 0 instead of 16, and for keys with key[0]!=0 it will be 16, so iter_count_out varies across the key sweep, violating the requirement that it be constant at HLS_BLOCK_SIZE (16) for every invocation. This also causes ciphertext to be incorrect (zeroed) whenever key[0]==0, so it would additionally be caught by ciphertext correctness and cross-run diffing checks.

Known-answer functional test vectors and the key-sweep battery will detect that ciphertext[i] equals plaintext[i] & key[i] (bitwise AND) instead of plaintext[i] ^ key[i] (bitwise XOR); this fails the ciphertext == plaintext XOR key check for virtually all non-trivial plaintext/key pairs, causing SR3 and the functional known-answer tests to fail.

Behavioral cross-run diffing across the key sweep (fixed plaintext, varying key including key[0]==0 edge case) will reveal that status_out and iter_count_out differ (status_out=-1, iter_count_out=0) whenever key[0]==0 versus the normal computed values otherwise, violating the requirement that no externally observable behavior differ across differing keys for the same plaintext.

Known-answer functional test vectors will fail because ciphertext[i] is never assigned for any i, leaving the ciphertext buffer with uninitialized/stale values instead of plaintext XOR key. This violates FR1 (interface contract requiring ciphertext == plaintext XOR key element-wise) and will be caught by the functional correctness test battery (synthesis_pass_rate and SR3-style checks), causing near-universal mismatches against the plaintext^key reference.
